votes.refutation: I first followed the router rather than assuming every unpinned queryset uses a replica. That assumption is true for Stamphog's separately routed product models, but false for these main-database settings/assignment models. A replica host alone is insufficient; the model must additionally appear in READ_REPLICA_OPT_IN or an explicit ALL_MODELS_USE_READ_REPLICA override. The claim supplies no evidence of either configuration for these classes. Pinning could protect a future/externally changed routing policy, but the alleged stale-toggle shipping path is not proved by the frozen source and defaults.

No frozen production configuration opts ReviewUserSettings into the replica. The claimed unconditional read-replica premise is therefore unproved; under the supplied configuration the toggle is read from the writer.
votes.refutation: I traced both the settings manager and actual router instead of equating an unpinned read with a replica read. The new Stamphog product does use a reader by default, but the ReviewUserSettings and reviewer-assignment models remain on the separately opt-in main-database routing policy. A deployment could introduce the hypothesized stale read by explicitly opting these models or all models into a replica, but the source provides no such production setting. Without that missing configuration fact, adding writer pinning is preventative hardening for a speculative trigger rather than a proved shipped opt-out bypass.
